title: Voter Registration
description: Citizens confirm eligibility, verify their constituency, and submit or update voter registration details before the rolls are frozen.
duration: Several weeks to several months before polling
keyFacts: In India, eligible citizens can register once they turn 18 through the Election Commission of India and state electoral offices.
Special summary revisions help correct names, addresses, photographs, and polling station assignments before an election.
Many democracies set a final registration deadline, while some permit same-day or automatic registration.
details: Collect identity, age, and residence proof as required in your jurisdiction.
Submit Form 6 in India for new voter enrolment, or the equivalent local process elsewhere.
Check the draft electoral roll and correct mistakes early to avoid election-day surprises.

title: Candidate Nomination
description: Political parties and independent candidates file nomination papers, affidavits, and deposits to enter the contest.
duration: Usually 7 to 14 days after election notification
keyFacts: Returning Officers scrutinize nomination papers to confirm that legal requirements are met.
Candidates in India must disclose criminal cases, assets, liabilities, and educational qualifications.
Other democracies may use primaries, party lists, or caucuses before final nomination.
details: Nomination papers are filed within the statutory window announced in the election schedule.
Objections can be raised during scrutiny if a candidate is ineligible or paperwork is incomplete.
Candidates can usually withdraw within a short withdrawal period before the final list is published.

title: Campaign Period
description: Candidates and parties present their agendas, seek public support, and campaign under rules meant to keep the contest fair.
duration: From final candidate list until campaigning closes
keyFacts: In India, the Model Code of Conduct limits misuse of government machinery, hate speech, and improper inducements.
Spending caps and disclosure rules are used in many systems to improve transparency.
Campaign silence periods close to polling help voters reflect without last-minute pressure.
details: Campaign material may include rallies, speeches, manifestos, media outreach, and door-to-door contact.
Observers and flying squads monitor possible violations such as bribery, misinformation, or intimidation.
Digital campaigns are increasingly regulated through ad disclosure and platform compliance rules.

title: Election Day Voting
description: Voters cast ballots at polling stations or through approved alternative methods such as postal or absentee ballots.
duration: One day in many countries, multiple phases in large democracies like India
keyFacts: Indian general elections may be held in several phases for security and logistics.
Polling officers verify voter identity, mark participation, and guide voters to cast a secret ballot.
Some countries offer early voting, mail voting, or extensive absentee options.
details: Polling stations open and close at notified hours, with voters in line at closing usually still allowed to vote.
India uses Electronic Voting Machines with VVPAT in parliamentary and assembly elections.
Accessibility measures may include ramps, Braille ballots, companions for eligible voters, and home voting in select cases.

title: Vote Counting & Verification
description: Ballots or machine records are counted, checked, and matched against seals, forms, and statutory procedures.
duration: Hours to multiple days depending on size and method
keyFacts: In India, EVM control units are opened under supervision on counting day and VVPAT slips may be verified as prescribed.
Postal ballots are often counted first in many jurisdictions.
Verification steps protect the integrity of totals before final declaration.
details: Counting agents of candidates observe the process and can raise objections through formal channels.
Round-wise counting sheets are prepared and signed to build a transparent trail.
Close races may trigger recount requests or mandatory audits in some democracies.

title: Results Declaration
description: Authorities publish constituency-wise results, confirm winners, and compile the overall verdict.
duration: Same day or shortly after counting concludes
keyFacts: Returning Officers formally declare the winner in each constituency after verifying the final totals.
Seat totals determine which party or coalition can attempt to form government.
Official websites and gazette notifications serve as authoritative sources for certified outcomes.
details: Media projections may appear early, but only official declarations are final.
Results dashboards often show vote share, turnout, margin of victory, and counting status.
Disputes can move into election petitions or court processes after declaration.

title: Oath Taking & Government Formation
description: The winning leader or coalition proves majority support, forms the executive, and begins the new term.
duration: A few days to a few weeks after results
keyFacts: In parliamentary systems, the head of state invites the leader most likely to command majority support.
Cabinets are formed after negotiations, party meetings, or coalition agreements.
The transition from results to governance is a constitutional step, not just a ceremonial event.
details: Winning representatives may receive certificates and complete formal seating procedures in the legislature.
The oath of office commits elected leaders to constitutional duties.
Hung parliaments can lead to coalition talks, support letters, or fresh mandates in some systems.
